examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
A binomial count uses a fixed number n of independent trials with a common success probability p. The mass choose(n,k)pᵏ(1−p)^(n−k) counts possible success positions. Indicator sums give mean np and variance np(1−p). Sampling without replacement generally introduces dependence and is hypergeometric instead. Translate exact, at least and at most carefully; complements often shorten tail calculations.

**Key relationship:** P(X=k)=C(n,k)pᵏ(1−p)ⁿ⁻ᵏ; E[X]=np; Var(X)=np(1−p)

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Verify fixed n, independence and equal p.
2. Translate the requested count event.
3. Use complements or indicator moments.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Recognize a fixed number n of independent equal-probability Bernoulli trials. Exactly k successes requires binomial(n,k)pᵏ(1−p)^(n−k); ‘at least one’ is often easier by complement. State whether trials are independent: drawing without replacement from a finite population is generally hypergeometric, not binomial.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A fair coin is tossed four times. What is the probability of exactly two heads?

**Answer: 0.375.** Choose the two head positions in binomial(4,2)=6 ways. Every ordered four-toss outcome has probability 1/16, so probability=6/16=0.375.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
The binomial coefficient is essential when any positions may succeed. Computing pᵏ(1−p)^(n−k) alone gives only one specified success pattern.

The coefficient C(n,k) counts different success positions; omitting it counts just one ordering.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

Binomial(10,0.2) has mean:

- **A.** 8
- **B.** 0.2
- **C.** 1.6
- **D.** 2

**Answer: D.** np=10·0.2=2. The value 1.6 is the variance.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Binomial assumptions include:

- **A.** Fixed trial count
- **B.** Independent trials
- **C.** Common success probability
- **D.** Always sampling without replacement

**Answer: A, B, C.** A/B/C define the model. Without-replacement sampling normally violates independence.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

Probability of exactly two heads in four independent fair tosses?



**Answer: 0.375.** choose(4,2)=6 sequences each have probability 1/16; total=6/16=0.375.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2025 CS1 · Q56 · NAT

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/binomial-distribution?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Binomial distribution. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Each bit survives unchanged with probability 1−0.01=0.99.
2. The five bit events are independent, and the whole message is error-free only if all five survive, so probability=0.99⁵=0.9509900499.
3. Rounding to three decimals gives **0.951**. The complement would be the probability of at least one flipped bit.
